comparison: Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the data accumulation claims (C1, C2, C34, C35, C48, C49, C50, C132). Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the app's success in rapidly gathering large volumes of data, with the editor noting 'great practical value' and no concerns raised about these metrics.

OpenEval finds data quality claims (C3, C4, C59-C66, C77, C78) supported with consistent metrics. Peer reviewers show mixed acceptance: they acknowledge high accuracy for birds, reptiles, mammals, and amphibians as a strength, but express concern about lower accuracy for seed plants, molluscs, and fishes, marking this as UNCERTAIN versus OpenEval's SUPPORTED.

Both agree that SDM improvement claims (C5, C67-C71, C82, C89) are supported. OpenEval notes statistical significance and appropriate methodology, while peer reviewers explicitly state the integration improves accuracy with implications for conservation planning. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED, though OpenEval notes the 50% proportion may not be fully optimized.

Complete agreement on endangered species claims (C6, C7, C72, C73, C98-C101). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find these SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers explicitly acknowledging improved accuracy for endangered species and emphasizing practical conservation value.

Both evaluations are UNCERTAIN about urban-natural gradient claims (C8, C51-C55, C84-C86). OpenEval notes low variance explained by PC1 (6.1%) and inferential causal links. Peer reviewers identify this as both strength and weakness, expressing concern that uniform distribution might not fully represent ecosystem diversity and could lead to model inaccuracies.

OpenEval finds taxonomic composition claims (C56, C57, C58) SUPPORTED with clear quantitative data. Peer reviewers also support the descriptive taxonomic composition (C56, C57) with no concerns raised, though peer review doesn't address the 45% filtering rate (C58).

OpenEval rates data quality mechanism claims (C79-C81) as UNCERTAIN due to inferential nature without direct experimental evidence. Peer reviewers support the app features and AI identification (C28-C33, C79-C81) as strengths contributing to effectiveness, showing more confidence in these mechanisms than OpenEval.

OpenEval finds optimal proportion claims (C74, C82, C83, C90, C91) SUPPORTED but notes the 50% fixed proportion may not be optimal. Peer review R3 addresses overlapping SDM claims (C82, C90) as part of broader support for SDM improvements, without specifically evaluating the optimal proportion findings.

Both agree on taxonomic variation in accuracy (C92-C97). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with well-documented variation but speculative mechanistic explanations. Peer reviewers also support this, acknowledging lower accuracy for certain taxa and accepting the authors' explanations without contestation.

Both support methodological limitation claims (C102-C108 for OpenEval; C104-C105 for peer review). OpenEval finds limitations honestly reported and not invalidating findings. Peer reviewers don't question the validation methodology, implicitly supporting the robustness claims.

OpenEval rates collaboration claims (C87, C88) as UNCERTAIN, noting no direct evidence linking government partnerships to spatial distribution patterns. Peer review R5 includes C88 in their UNCERTAIN evaluation of urban-natural gradient claims, sharing concern about the causal relationship.

OpenEval rates application claims (C109-C127) as UNCERTAIN due to speculative and inferential nature, representing future possibilities rather than demonstrated outcomes. Peer reviewers are more positive (SUPPORTED), emphasizing conservation applications and stakeholder engagement as strengths, though they evaluate a subset of claims (C36, C110-C113, C115, C127-C129).

OpenEval rates broader impact claims (C128-C131) as UNCERTAIN, noting no evidence of actual collaboration outcomes or societal impacts. Peer review R11 includes C128-C129 in their SUPPORTED evaluation, viewing stakeholder engagement positively, showing divergence in confidence about these claims.

OpenEval finds methodological details (C133-C152) SUPPORTED as clearly documented and following best practices. Peer review R7 addresses a subset of methods (C135-C136, C140-C142) as part of supporting the app's innovative approach and AI features, with no methodological concerns raised.

Peer reviewers express UNCERTAIN evaluation about spatial and taxonomic biases (C26, C27, C44-C47), raising concerns about whether biases in community-sourced data are adequately addressed. OpenEval does not have a corresponding result specifically evaluating these bias-related claims.
